Feature: Supports Rivermax Generic and Media APIs
Description: By default, it supports generic APIs, but media API can be enabled by setting sdp-file property.

Feature: Supports any type of RTP packet (Compressed, Uncompressed, audio etc.) with Generic APIs
Description: No restriction on content of RTP payload in case of Generic APIs.

Feature: Supports RTCP packets,In addition to RTP
Description: RTCP packets can also be transmitted.

Feature: Traffic shaping in case of Uncompressed streams (video and audio)
Description: By using Rivermax media APIs,packet pacing can be enabled for uncompressed video and audio streams.
Uncompressed SMPTE 2110-20 streams with packet pacing is supported through Rivermax media APIs.
Uncompressed SMPTE 2110-30 stream with packet pacing is supported through Rivermax media APIs.

Feature: Supports RTP packetization of uncompressed video
Description: Uncompressed video as input can be converted to RTP packets as per SMPTE 2110-20 before sending to network

Feature: Supports RTP packetization of uncompressed audio
Description: Uncompressed audio as input can be converted to RTP packets as per SMPTE 2110-30 before sending to network
"In addition to system clock hardware clock from the PTP source (Network card) can be used to generate RTP packet timestamp"
Separate thread to packetize and transmit the data. This thread can be bound to specific CPU core(s)
Rivermax media API's will allocate GPU memory to receive the SMPTE 2110-20 stream and this memory is directly accessible by NIC (ConnectX 6 or above required)
By using Rivermax media API's, can transmit redundant packet streams over independent network paths. SDP file will decide whether it is 2022-7 stream

Transmit SMPTE 291M ancillary data (e.g. CEA-608/708 closed captions) over ST 2110 networks. Accepts meta/x-st-2038 caps and packetizes ST2038 buffers into RFC 8331 RTP payloads. SMPTE 2022-7 redundancy is supported.
